data.title: JOYY's Multi-engine Strategy Supports Steady Total Revenue Growth in Q3 2026
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JOYY Inc. () ("JOYY" or the "Company"), a leading global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

JOYY maintained its growth momentum in the third quarter, with total revenues reaching US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Social Entertainment revenue totaled US$441 million, up 8.8% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. BIGO Ads generated US$145.7 million in revenue, marking increases of 39.6% year over year and 9% quarter over quarter. SHOPLINE revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10% quarter over quarter. Driven by the multi-engine growth strategy, the contribution from non-livestreaming revenue further increased to 32.8% of total revenues this quarter.

The Company maintained a solid financial position in the third quarter. Non-GAAP[1] operating income reached US$46.6 million, representing an increase of 14.6% year over year. Non-GAAP[1] EBITDA amounted to US$55.7 million, up 10.1% year over year. Operating cash inflow totaled US$102.2 million for the quarter, while the Company's net cash position stood at US$2.94 billion as of September 30, 2026.

JOYY continued to execute its shareholder return program, reinforcing its commitment to delivering long-term value to shareholders. From the beginning of 2026 to November 13, the Company returned a total of US$536 million to shareholders through share repurchases of US$319.8 million and dividend payments of US$216.2 million, progressing toward its target of returning US$1.5 billion cumulatively to shareholders by the end of 2028.

[1] This press release includes certain non-GAAP financial measures as additional clarifying items to aid investors in further understanding the Company's performance and the impact that these items and events had on the financial results. The non-GAAP financial measures provided above should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP. For details of the non-GAAP measures, including the reconciliations of GAAP measures to non-GAAP measures, please refer to the press release titled "JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results" issued by the Company on November 19, 2026.

data.title: ANT Stock’s Debut Could Be A Blockbuster – But SpaceX And SK Hynix History Shows Why The First-Day Pop Isn’t Everything
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gray market insights suggest that investors were still lining up to buy the stock.
  • Mega listings this year, including SpaceX and SK Hynix, have mostly disappointed new shareholders.
  • Anthropic stock will begin trading on Thursday under the ticker ‘ANT.’

Anthropic PBC’s shares are expected to open between 20% and 26% higher in gray market trading, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, another bullish signal of breakneck demand for the AI firm’s shares after its record $107.3-billion initial public offering (IPO).

Derivatives offered by online brokerage IG International pointed to a market value of $1.35 trillion on Thursday morning in Hong Kong, implying a gain of more than 24% from the IPO price of $83, according to the report. Anthropic-tied perpetual futures contracts listed on the crypto platform Hyperliquid traded at around $100, a 20% premium to the IPO price.

Anthropic on Wednesday said it sold shares at $83 apiece, sharply higher than the $70 to $78 range it indicated earlier. The IPO was reportedly oversubscribed seven times and received bids worth about $500 billion.

The gray market insights suggest that investors were still lining up to buy the stock on Thursday, when it begins trading on Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ‘ANT.’

A potential first-day rally in ANT would further allay concerns about global AI demand and cement Anthropic’s status as an AI bellwether. Still, doubts remain about whether Anthropic will have an easy ride in the near future.

Anthropic IPO: Challenge Ahead

Mega listings this year, including SpaceX (SPCX) and SK Hynix (SKHY), have mostly disappointed new shareholders, according to a Morningstar analysis.

SpaceX began trading at $150 a share, an 11% premium to its offering price, in June. In the 110 trading days since SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO, shares have closed below $150 on 74 occasions. SpaceX has spent more than 50% of its time as a public company, or 60 days, trading below its opening price.

SK Hynix and Cerebras (CBRS) also currently trade well below their IPO price.

The sheer amount of new stock available to public investors is likely hindering performance, according to Ben Inker, co-head of asset allocation at GMO. Historically, “when you got a lot of supply in the form of IPOs, that tended to harm the market,” he said, according to Morningstar.

SK Hynix’s ANT Stake Swells 16 Times

Bloomberg reported that SK Hynix unit SK Telecom’s investment in Anthropic generated nearly 16-times returns and is now worth $3.2 billion. The company first invested in 2023. SK Hynix and rival Samsung Electronics are also investors in Anthropic.

For Samsung and SK Hynix, the upside is supply. Anthropic’s prospectus names the two Korean chipmakers along with Micron as the primary manufacturers of the high-bandwidth and other high-performance memory used in AI infrastructure.

In an explainer earlier this week, Stocktwits detailed Anthropic’s major backers who stand to benefit from its IPO.

Anthropic’s IPO Details, Retail View

Anthropic issued 801.3 million new shares and selling shareholders sold 23.6 million shares in the IPO. The company priced the sale at $83 apiece on Wednesday, raising a total of $107.3 billion, including $26 billion through a private placement.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for ANT was at nearly the highest mark in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone (98/100), with traders speculating that the stock would surely touch $100 on Thursday.

data.title: Singapore’s MAS issues $77 million in tokenized bills settled via CBDC
data.description:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced Thursday that it issued S$100 million ($77.5 million) of four-week tokenized MAS Bills on Nov. 6, as the country steps up its tokenization drive.

In a statement released Thursday, the central bank said the bills were issued natively on its Singapore Dollar Test Network and settled in wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC). The bills will mature on Dec. 4.

Notably, five primary dealers — DBS Bank, HSBC, OCBC, UOB, and Standard Chartered — participated in the auction, which drew applications more than twice the issuance size.

The issuance builds on the 2025 live trial of interbank overnight lending transactions settled via wholesale CBDC. "This paves the way for secured lending transactions involving tokenized assets to take place on the Singapore Dollar Test Network," the MAS said.

The Singapore Dollar Test Network is a shared ledger infrastructure that enables financial institutions to test the settlement of tokenized financial assets using wholesale CBDC, according to the statement. It will be renamed to SG Digital Ledger, the MAS said.

"The live issuance allowed us to test a new method of issuance, and further enhance our in-house distributed ledger infrastructure," said Chia Der Jiun, Managing Director of MAS.

Scaling tokenized bills

In the next phase, the MAS plans to scale tokenized MAS Bills, expand their use for collateral management, and onboard more institutions.

"MAS aims to demonstrate how tokenized securities can be used more widely in mainstream financial market activities, potentially achieving greater settlement efficiencies in the process," said the central bank.

In an accompanying statement released Thursday, Lim Soon Chong, group head of global transaction services at DBS Bank, said that the initiative has provided "greater confidence" for financial institutions to transact in tokenized assets.

"Over time, more robust infrastructure can help catalyze trading activity and deepen liquidity, supporting the progression of tokenized assets from issuance and experimentation toward more active secondary markets," said Lim.

Tokenization push

The issuance comes as Singaporean financial institutions accelerate their adoption of tokenized assets, with MAS' Chia saying that tokenization has "moved beyond experiments."

On Thursday, Standard Chartered announced an expansion of its tokenized deposits solution to enable near real-time transactions across Singapore and Hong Kong. The bank said eligible clients can now utilize commercial bank deposits within digital treasury and investment workflows.

Meanwhile, StraitsX, OCBC, and Standard Chartered said Thursday that they have completed a proof-of-concept testing interoperability between tokenized deposit networks issued by different banks.

Earlier this week, DBS Bank and Kinexys by JPMorgan also launched an interoperability solution designed to enable institutions to make instant, around-the-clock transfers of USD tokenized deposits between the U.S. and Singapore.

data.title: Holding firm Exor to raise bioMerieux stake to around 8.5%
data.description:
Investment company Exor said on Thursday it was raising its stake in bioMérieux to 8.53% from 3.87%, with the aim of becoming a long-term investor, citing confidence in the French biotechnology firm.

The transaction will be carried out through an exchange of Exor's shares and voting rights in Institut Mérieux for those in bioMérieux. Institut Mérieux will remain bioMérieux's majority shareholder with 55.24% of the share capital and 68.67% of voting rights.

  • The deal is expected to be completed in December, with Exor set to increase its voting rights in bioMérieux to 5.35%

  • The investment arm of Italy's Agnelli family currently holds a 10% stake and 5.3% of voting rights in Institut Mérieux

  • After completion of the deal, it will hold 5.02% of Institut Merieux's shares and 2.58% of voting rights

  • Exor values bioMerieux greatly for its leadership in diagnostics and wants to support it over the long term, CEO John Elkann said

data.title: Bitcoin ETF assets fall to three-month low as 2026 net outflows top $2.5B
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) ended Wednesday with $77.7 billion in net assets, a three-month low, as net outflows for the year topped $2.5 billion.

The funds recorded $306.4 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to SoSoValue data. The funds held about 1.25 million Bitcoin (BTC) at Wednesday’s close, according to Walet Pilot.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) held the most Bitcoin, with about 779,870 BTC, followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) with 172,080 BTC and Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC) with 122,730 BTC.

Bitcoin briefly dipped below $63,000 on Wednesday. It traded at $63,545 at publishing time, down 1.7% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of crypto exchange Giottus, said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph that institutional selling and expectations of tighter US monetary policy continued to weigh on market sentiment.

He also cited onchain data showing that long-term Bitcoin holders had reduced their positions by around 121,151 BTC over 30 days.

Selling pressure also extended to US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs, which recorded around $40 million in outflows Wednesday, bringing their 2026 net withdrawals to roughly $895 million.

data.title: Energean profit jumps 54% on higher oil prices as Katlan project stays on track
data.description:
The Israel-based Eastern Mediterranean gas producer said net profit for the nine months to Sept. 30 rose to $317m from $206m a year earlier. The increase was driven by a 44% rise in realised liquids prices to $88 a barrel, reflecting stronger oil market conditions during the period.

Operational performance remained solid, with average production of 139,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (kboed), in line with the company's guidance. Adjusted EBITDAX rose 7% to $888m, while production costs excluding royalties fell 10% to $193m, supporting profitability.

Energean maintained its production outlook for the full year of 130-140 kboed and said the Katlan offshore gas development in Israel remains on track to deliver first gas in the first half of 2027. Total development expenditure for the project is expected to be around $1.25bn, with the company having secured a $700m 10-year loan to support financing.

The London-listed group also reaffirmed its commitment to shareholder returns, declaring a third-quarter dividend of $0.10 per share and saying it expects to return about $110m to shareholders in 2026.

Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com

data.title: Swiss Trade Surplus Grows In October
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Switzerland's foreign trade surplus increased in October as exports grew faster than imports, data from the Federal Customs Administration showed on Thursday.

The trade surplus climbed to CHF 3.2 billion in October from CHF 1.2 billion in September.

In real terms, exports climbed 2.4 percent monthly in October, and imports were 0.7 percent higher.

Exports of chemicals and pharmaceutical products-key sectors for Switzerland's economy-grew 11.2 percent in October. Watch exports, another major Swiss industry, rose 4.6 percent. On the import side, Switzerland brought in 18.5 percent fewer jewelry items.

Separate official data from the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry showed that watch exports rose 9.1 percent annually in October, driven largely by increased demand for steel and bimetallic watches.

data.title: Bitcoin, Ether Recover as Traders Digest Fed Rate-Hike Signals
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin and ether rebounded Thursday after slipping earlier following the release of the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, which came out hawkish.

Bitcoin was 1.9% higher at $63,442 after tumbling as low as $62,086 in the previous session, while ether rose 2.2% to $1,801.50. The minutes showed that almost all Fed officials supported further rate hikes, with a handful considering an increase of half a percentage point in December.

Rate hikes increase the opportunity cost of holding nonyielding assets, including cryptocurrencies, as bonds become relatively more attractive. Traders are pricing a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike in December, with a 10% chance of a half-point rise, according to CME FedWatch.

Crypto investors now turn to Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering, with the company's shares expected to list Thursday. Some market participants attributed bitcoin's latest slide to investors channeling funds out of crypto assets and into the Claude developer's flotation.

"Given the investment profile, this type of allocation usually falls in the same bucket as bitcoin, and it would be consistent with investors selling bitcoin into weakness to make room," said Mauricio Di Bartolomeo, co-founder of bitcoin lending platform Ledn.

Write to Joseph Wilkins at joseph.wilkins@wsj.com

data.title: Johnson Matthey H1 Pre-Tax Profit Falls; Raises FY Underlying Operating Profit Outlook; Ups Dividend
data.description:
LONDON (dpa-AFX) - Johnson Matthey Plc (JMAT.L), a speciality chemicals and sustainable technologies company, Thursday reported lower pre-tax profit from continuing operations for the first half, despite higher revenue, mainly due to impairment charges on investments in associates and financial assets. The company also raised its full-year outlook for underlying operating profit.

Profit before tax from continuing operations declined to £15 million from £86 million a year ago.

The company recorded impairment charges of £63 million on investments in associates and £62 million on financial assets, compared with no such charges in the prior-year period.

Excluding one-time items, underlying pre-tax profit rose 47% to £162 million from £110 million last year.

Net loss from continuing operations was £15 million or 11.8p per share, compared with £16 million or 12.7p per share loss a year ago.

Underlying profit from continuing operations increased to £129 million or 102.2p per basic share from £86 million or 68.2p per basic share last year.

Including discontinued operations, the company reported net profit of £335 million or 262.5 pence per share, compared with a loss of £18 million or 14.2 pence per share a year ago.

Operating profit rose to £170 million from £117 million last year, while underlying operating profit climbed 32% to £187 million.

Revenue increased 35% to £7.206 billion from £5.353 billion in the previous year.

The Board approved an interim dividend of 22.7p per share, up 3% from 22p per share a year ago, payable on February 2, to shareholders on record as of November 27.

For the full year, the company now expects group underlying operating profit to grow at a high single-digit percentage rate, compared with its previous outlook for low- to mid-single-digit growth, at constant precious metal prices and constant currency.

On the LSE, Johnson Matthey shares closed down 1.28% at 2,320p on Wednesday.

data.title: UK's Royal Mail taps finance chief Ablin as CEO amid calls for parcel market reforms
data.description:
Royal Mail owner International Distribution Services (IDS) named finance chief Paul Ablin as the British postal group's new CEO on Thursday, while renewing its warning that the firm is competing on an "unlevel playing field" against rivals in the parcels market.

Royal Mail's current CEO Alistair Cochrane will retire at the end of 2026, with Ablin taking over from January 2027.

The more than 500-year-old company, whose iconic red post boxes with the Royal Crest dot Britain, has been repeatedly probed and fined over missed delivery targets by UK regulators, as it also struggles with falling letter volumes.

In October, Royal Mail implemented a Universal Service reform to address the issues and announced plans to cut up to 2,500 jobs by the end of 2027.

"We welcome the Government’s plans to tackle bogus self-employment and will continue to push for strong and enforceable standards across the industry," IDS chief Martin Seidenberg said in a statement.

Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle said the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms that did not employ staff under the same conditions and urged the British government to act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail, a BBC report said on Tuesday.

Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky's EP Group closed its acquisition of IDS in June 2025 after committing to protect Royal Mail and its workers and customers.

IDS forecast that Royal Mail’s second-half performance will be hurt by the delay to some mail price increases that were due to take effect last month.

While Royal Mail revenue rose 3.9% to £4.13 billion ($5.42 billion) in the six months to September 27 and parcel volumes grew 8%, addressed letter volumes were down 8% in the period.

data.title: Gigasun signs a new order in China worth approximately 67 MSEK
data.description:
Gigasun's wholly owned subsidiary in China has signed a new agreement with a logistics company. The agreement concerns the installation of a solar power plant with a total capacity of approximately 6.8 megawatts (MW) in Guangdong Province.

The facility is expected to generate annual revenues of approximately 3.4 MSEK from electricity sales. This corresponds to a total order value of approximately 68 MSEK over the 20-year term of the agreement.

The investment in the facility amounts to approximately 26.4 MSEK, and the project is planned to start during the fourth quarter of 2026. The facility will be owned and operated by Gigasun's subsidiary and is expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 3,300 tons per year.

The project is fully commercially viable without the need for government subsidies.

CEO Max Metelius comments:

New projects are now being signed at a time when we have significantly reduced our financing costs, which increases the selection of profitable projects and makes every new megawatt more valuable to shareholders. We can also note that solar irradiation in October was back to normal levels after a third quarter affected by unusually low irradiation.

For more information, please contact:

Max Metelius, CEO Gigasun AB (publ)

Phone: +46 (0) 72 316 04 44

E-mail: max.metelius@gigasun.se

Stefan Salomonsson, CFO Gigasun AB (publ)

Phone: +46 (0) 70 220 80 00

E-mail: stefan.salomonsson@gigasun.se

Certified Advisor is FNCA Sweden AB

About the operation

Gigasun operates in China through its wholly owned subsidiaries Advanced Soltech Renewable Energy (Hangzhou) Co. Ltd (“ASRE”) and Longrui Solar Energy (Suqian) Co. Ltd. (“SQ”), and Suqian Ruiyan New Energy Co., Ltd. (“RY”).

The business model consists of financing, installing, owning and managing solar PV installations on customers' roofs in China. The customer does not pay for the solar PV installation, but instead enters an agreement to buy the electricity that the solar PV installation produces under a 20-year agreement. Current income comes from the sale of electricity to customers and governmental subsidies.

The goal is to have an installed capacity of 1,000 megawatts (MW) in the medium term.

data.title: Historically 'Normal' Rates Improve Fixed-Income Return Prospects — Market Talk
data.description: Rates are back to historically "normal" levels, improving fixed income's long-term return prospects, PGIM Credit's Robert Tipp says in a note. Still, yields may have not yet peaked, keeping the chief investment strategist cautious on long duration. Following the recent upward shift, it is possible that rates reached restrictive levels that could conceivably bring inflation to heel, he says. "Yet, given this cycle is host of upward drivers for growth and inflation, our suspicion is that another stair-step higher for the developed market yield curve may be required to bring inflation back down to target," Tipp says. However, it may take some time for central banks and markets to make that call, he adds. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

A/S Motortramp participates in NORDEN’s share buy-back program by selling shares pro rata in order to maintain the current ownership of just under 32% of the shares in NORDEN.
